simple.meaning: סְעַד (çᵉʻad) is a Hebrew action word meaning “to aid.” BibleIQ anchors the English reading to this source verb before comparing its uses.
simple.biblicalBackground: This action appears 1 time in Ezra, beginning at Ezra 5:2. The surrounding contexts include family line, prophetic witness.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to סְעַד (H5583) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: Actions in Scripture show what people do, what God does, and how covenant faithfulness or rebellion is described. BibleIQ compares the action across its occurrences.
simple.summary: סְעַד (çᵉʻad) / H5583 is traced through Ezra 5:2 with source-language evidence and verse context.

definitions.full: H5583. sead [ סְעַד ] verb Pa`el support, sustain ( ᵑ7 Zinjirli; see Biblical Hebrew); — Participle active plural לְהוֺן מְסַעֲדִין Ezra 5:2 .

occurrences.englishText: Then Zerubbabel the son of Shealtiel, and Jeshua the son of Jozadak rose up and began to build God’s house which is at Jerusalem; and with them were the prophets of God, helping them.
